Likelihood: the target event requires three things: (a) a start-up demand within the 30-operating-day horizon, with the number of demands unknown; (b) omission of the bypass step despite a written procedure, generically about 1E-3 to 1E-2 per demand and possibly higher during commissioning; and (c) progression of that error to actual internal damage. With no diagnostic trend, verified initiating fault or confirmed occurrence (P3), the point estimate is about 1%, with a plausible range of roughly 0.1 to 3%. Predictability: the mechanism was foreseeable because it is documented as a HAZOP cause. However, no precursor signalled occurrence within this specific window, so occurrence predictability is low (15%). Qualitative risk: low likelihood over the horizon; severity is undetermined, so the ranking is provisional. Negligence: none attributable on pre-decision evidence. The hazard was identified and a safeguard was listed, and no ignored warning, deficient procedure or non-compliance was evidenced. Recommendations: verify that the start-up procedure explicitly requires bypass opening, with a hold point and independent sign-off or checklist. Cover this step in the pre-start-up review and operator briefing. Evaluate bypass position indication or a start-up permissive to reduce reliance on a single administrative control.
